findings.summary: The export materializes one row per conversion document without enforcing EXCEL_MAX_ROWS. Exact evidence projects 1,807,231 rows, exceeding Excel's 1,048,576-row worksheet limit, so the default single-sheet export cannot satisfy the capacity requirement and may also exhaust browser memory while flatMap builds the full array.
EXCEL_MAX_ROWS is declared but never used; there is no capacity check, aggregation, pagination, or bounded fallback before writeSingleBrowserWorksheet is called.

unverified: No tests are shown for worksheet-capacity boundaries, browser memory behavior, download completion, or reconciliation of exported annual-report totals.
The definitions and behavior of Lot and writeSingleBrowserWorksheet are not supplied, so type correctness and writer-side overflow/error handling cannot be verified.

findings.summary: displayedClosing subtracts only expense and fx_eur consumption, omitting the supported fx_other category. Given the observed fx_other total of 1,494,440 TRY, the displayed closing balance is overstated by exactly 1,494,440 TRY and cannot reconcile for pools containing fx_other consumption.
The change exposes only a computed closing value; it does not display or return the required exact opening, inflow, per-consumer-category outflow/conversion, and closing turnover.

unverified: No tests are shown proving exact reconciliation across expense, fx_eur, fx_other, mixed-consumption, empty-consumption, or fractional TRY cases.
The definitions of Pool and sum are not supplied, so type correctness, missing-value handling, and numerical precision/rounding behavior cannot be verified.

findings.summary: Each detail amount is rounded independently, so rounding residuals are neither measured nor assigned to a detail row. Consequently the returned amounts can differ from the currency-rounded source total, directly violating exact reconciliation; the reported 1578 TRY aggregate drift demonstrates material impact.

The implementation uses binary floating-point multiplication and Math.round without converting inputs to integer minor units or defining currency/tie-rounding semantics, so decimal boundary cases can round unexpectedly.

The function does not validate that source and shares are finite, that shares are nonnegative, or that shares sum to the required whole; malformed inputs can produce NaN, Infinity, negative allocations, or totals unrelated to the source.

unverified: No tests are shown for positive and negative sources, zero values, fractional-cent boundaries, residual distribution, invalid shares, or exact reconciliation across many detail rows.
The intended currency rounding mode, supported currency precision, and contract for shares that do not sum to one are not specified in the supplied text.

findings.summary: The verify script no longer runs `prisma generate`, so generated clients are not refreshed before typecheck after schema changes.
The `|| echo existing Prisma mismatch` fallback converts every non-zero TypeScript result into a successful script exit, allowing genuine typecheck failures to pass the release gate.
A temporary reviewer-only debug probe is added to the release tree despite the frozen acceptance criterion excluding reviewer probes.
Private review-run scratch notes are added to the release tree despite the frozen acceptance criterion excluding private root-cause notes.
